description: The same recipient with leading and trailing whitespace and mixed case, and no angle brackets, collapses to the plain-lowercase first-send delivery key.
why_it_exists: normEmail() only reaches its .trim() through the raw branch when the address carries no angle brackets - the bracket match already discards surrounding whitespace, so wf4-delivery-key-recipient-normalisation never exercises it. A pasted address commonly arrives padded: a spreadsheet cell, a copied signature block, a Telegram forward. Untrimmed, " insurerclaims01@example.com " hashes to a different send_key than the same address without the padding, the delivery looks new, and the same letter goes out twice. This case pins the trim and the lowercase together on the unbracketed path.

input.sanitisation_note: The address is the same 27-character synthetic address used by wf4-delivery-key-first-send and wf4-delivery-key-recipient-normalisation, with mixed case and two spaces of padding on each side. No real recipient appears here.

assertions: send_key is identical to the plain-lowercase first-send key
normEmail() trims leading and trailing whitespace from an address with no angle brackets
the channel is uppercased before entering the basis
